# PR #1280 — delta re-review at the merged head `2386aed3`

**Head `2386aed3b75ad7db785e9dfcda65422a8642cef6` (merged into `auctions` as `ea7b4b12`, 2026-09-24T23:56Z). PR author `felixfelix-bot`; this hardening commit is authored by the maintainer `Maximoto <maximotodev@proton.me>`.** This delta is exactly one commit since my last review at `04bdc1d8` (id 5308176776): `2386aed3` "fix(auctions): harden rebid collateral validation", 6 files +773/−228.

Reviewer `felixfelix-bot` (bot, automated), model `glm-5.3`, family `zhipu`. Citations are `file:line` at `2386aed3` unless another ref is named.

## The carried RISK is closed — and closed properly

My last two reviews carried one open [RISK]: cross-bidder `prev_bid` chains defeated the DLEQ delta binding (`computeLegLockedAmounts` trusted any resolvable parent, so a 1-sat attacker child citing a victim's leg as `prev_bid` inherited the victim's cumulative amount with real 1-sat proofs, won canonical selection, and wedged settlement). This commit deletes that entire class of trust:

- **`computeLegLockedAmounts` is gone.** Nothing mutates `bid.legLockedAmount` anymore; the parse-time placeholder (cumulative, `src/lib/schemas/auction/bidEvent.ts:147`) is never laundered into a delta.
- **`verifyBidCollateralChain` (bidValidation.ts:283-357)** now derives economic authority independently: same bidder (`:302`), same auction root + coordinate (`:303-304`), bounded walk (256 legs, `MAX_COLLATERAL_CHAIN_LENGTH`, `:273`; cycle-safe via the `seen` id-set, `:298`), per-ancestor `validateBid` structural re-check (`:312-314`), and — decisive — **per-leg DLEQ at the exact required delta** (`verifyBidDleqWithKeysets` with `legDelta: requiredAmount`, `:349`). A cross-author or unresolvable parent is `invalid` (`:319`), not inherited.
- **Cumulative credit now requires real collateral for every sat.** The prior attack's core — 1-sat DLEQ verifiably backing a 100,001-sat claim — is exactly what the new test `"same-author poison parent cannot subsidize a directly confirmed 1-sat child"` (computeValidatedBids.test.ts) kills, and `"cross-author parent cannot contribute monetary credit to an attacker child"` covers the cross-bidder variant I described.
- **NUT-7 spend is now per-leg** (`hasDisqualifyingSpentLeg`, bidValidation.ts:583-586): a spent ancestor invalidates the descendant's credit unless post-settlement-excused for that exact leg — the pre-existing "root spent ⇒ child still wins on victim's coins" gap closes with it.
- **Every settlement/walk consumer reads the trusted chain, not the placeholder**: `settlementDescriptor.ts:209` (adapter copy, deliberately not mutating the parsed event), `winNotification.ts:132-152` (per-leg `expectedTokenAmount`), `deriveState`'s release filter, and seller readiness now requires the complete root-to-winner release chain (`hasCompleteTrustedReleaseChain`, `settlementDescriptor.ts:468` — flips the old "only the top leg's release" acceptance, with the test expectation changed accordingly).
- **The old M3 backward-propagation block is removed.** Verdicts are strictly per-bid now; ancestors get structural + DLEQ verification but no synthesized quorum. This is the correct narrowing — the deleted code's own LIMITATION comment (old bidValidation.ts:371) admitted it was unsound if validators don't validate the full chain.

The AUCTIONS.md §539-546 claim ("enforced by the selection algorithm and the seller's settlement walk") is now true in the tree: the selection surface enforces same-bidder/same-auction/strictly-increasing at the collateral-authority layer.

## What I verified mechanically

- **The PR's cumulative diff does not touch the server validator** (`src/server/auction-validator/` absent from the 50-file list). The server's own `deriveBidLegAmount` (lifecycle.ts:348-354) resolves any parent without a same-bidder check — identical code at the PR base `d0542215`, so pre-existing upstream behavior, out of this PR's scope. Worth an upstream follow-up for consistency with the client's stricter derivation.
- **Ran the touched suites locally at this head**: `bun test --isolate` on `computeValidatedBids.test.ts` + `auctionWon.test.ts` + `settlementDescriptor.test.ts` → 124 pass / 0 fail (310 expects), with the 256-leg chain test the slowest at ~5s against bun's default 5s per-test cap; re-run of `computeValidatedBids.test.ts` with `--timeout 60000` → **50/50 pass** including all four chain-authority attacks. CI's `unit-integration` at this head is green (1810 pass / 130 files, 0 fail, run 36072415291).
- **CI at head, read live from the API**: `unit-integration` ✅ 1810 pass + 16 integration pass; `e2e-grep` ✅ 199 passed (12.4m), 1 flaky retried (`auction-settlement.spec.ts:821`, the relay-publish flake); prettier / footprint / auctions-surface / security-scan ✅; e2e-full skipped (dispatch-only).
- **Carried R2 (stale PR body) resolved**: the body now reads "current head `2386aed3`" and cites this head's runs.
- **The open sign-off item (ADR-0012 attribution) is closed by the maintainer's own approval** (maximotodev, id 5311651893, at this head: "I ratify ADR-0012 for this merge and accept the existing historical attribution record as sufficient provenance").
- **Deleted-code audit**: repo-wide grep confirms `computeLegLockedAmounts` has zero remaining code references (its only textual appearance is the stale `bidEvent.ts:67` comment flagged below); the only consumers of `legLockedAmount` outside the new trusted-chain adapters are the seller's first-party publish walk (`publish/auctions.tsx:774,1458` — local records where the field is the true locked amount by construction) and the validator's own `deriveBidLegAmount` seam (above).

## Residual notes (non-blocking, post-merge)

- **[NIT] `src/lib/schemas/auction/bidEvent.ts:67`** — the placeholder comment still says the field is "ALWAYS overwritten by `computeLegLockedAmounts`", a function this commit deleted. One-line comment fix.
- **[NIT] `src/server/auction-validator/lifecycle.ts:348-354`** — `deriveBidLegAmount` still credits deltas across a cross-bidder parent (pre-existing, untouched by this PR; noted above for upstream consistency).
- **[INFO] `MAX_COLLATERAL_CHAIN_LENGTH = 256`** (bidValidation.ts:273) bounds the walk and the test pins 256-ok/257-invalid. Each leg still requires a real DLEQ-verified amount, so the bound is a complexity guard, not an economic one — fine as is.

## Verdict

**APPROVED** — no change requests at this head. The one carried [RISK] is genuinely closed with the right architecture (per-leg cryptographic authority instead of inherited trust), the test suite attacks the exact chains a reviewer would build, and the maintainer's ratification plus green current-head CI close the remaining merge conditions. This is a post-merge delta review: `2386aed3` was the merge head, recorded here for the tip-coverage trail.

— gate-1 delta re-review at `2386aed3b75ad7db785e9dfcda65422a8642cef6`; cold cross-family audit (gate 2.5) run before posting and its corrections applied.
